#### 3. Cline #13552, #13515: Stop showing cost estimates for subscription-billed providers (LOW/SKIP)

- **What**: VS Code webview + CLI fix preventing subscription-billed providers (ChatGPT Plus/Pro via openai-codex, ClinePass, Claude Code) from showing API-rate cost estimates that users read as real charges on top of their subscription. Providers marked `metadata.usageCostDisplay = \"subscription\"` in the SDK now suppress dollar figures in task headers and model pricing rows. The webview hook returns full tri-state `\"show\" | \"hide\" | \"subscription\"` union, cost renders only when `=== \"show\"` (matching CLI's shouldShowCliUsageCost policy), and the hook returns `\"unknown\"` while ListProviders is in-flight to suppress flashing estimates on chat-view mount.
- **Why**: Subscription users saw misleading cost figures computed from API-rate catalog pricing, not actual charges.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13552 (stop showing cost estimates for subscription-billed providers), https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13515 (hide task costs on vscode when ClinePass is selected)
- **Category**: provider (integration/UI)
- **Size**: LOW (Cline VS Code webview feature + ClinePass/ChatGPT subscription billing integration — Alexi has NO subscription billing, NO ClinePass, NO per-provider usageCostDisplay tri-state UI logic, Alexi src/core/costTracker.ts L1-200 tracks token usage and computes dollar estimates from catalog pricing with NO subscription exemptions, pattern only relevant if Alexi adds subscription-billed providers where users pay flat-rate and cost display should suppress API-rate estimates, SKIP for now).

#### 6. Cline #13521: Platform-native line endings for new files (ALREADY IMPLEMENTED IN ALEXI)

- **What**: The write_file tool now uses platform-native EOL (os.EOL) for new files instead of hardcoded `\n`. Prevents CRLF/LF mismatches on Windows where new files created by the agent had Unix line endings even though the project used Windows line endings, causing git diffs to show the entire file changed. Shared helper `normalizeNewFileLineEndings` replaces `\n` with `os.EOL`.
- **Why**: Cross-platform correctness — new files should match the platform's native EOL convention.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13521 (create new files with platform-native line ending)
- **Category**: tool (write)
- **Size**: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED (Alexi src/tool/eol-normalizer.ts L1-66 exists with `normalizeNewFileLineEndings(content: string, eol: LineEnding = getPlatformEol()): string` L36-45 replacing `\n` with `os.EOL`, `preserveExistingLineEndings(newContent: string, existingContent: string): string` L51-58 preserving existing file EOL when overwriting, `detectLineEnding(content: string): LineEnding` L25-27 sniffing CRLF vs LF; src/tool/tools/write.ts L89-97 uses `normalizeNewFileLineEndings(finalContent)` for new files and `preserveExistingLineEndings(finalContent, existingText)` for existing files — same pattern as Cline #13521, already complete, SKIP).

#### 7. Cline #13525: Prevent search_codebase from crashing on giant single-line files (ALREADY SAFE IN ALEXI)

- **What**: Cline's search_codebase tool's ripgrep JSON mode handler buffered all of `rg --json` stdout into one string. Each JSON event embeds the full matched line (--max-columns is ignored in JSON mode), so searching directories with serialized trace dumps (single-line multi-hundred-MB JSON files) accumulated gigabytes of stdout until string concatenation threw RangeError: Out of memory, killing the process (uncaught exception outside tool try/catch). Now stops buffering past 10MB, drops trailing partial events before parsing, and truncates context lines to MAX_LINE_CHARS.
- **Why**: Defensive coding — tools should not crash the process via OOM on legitimate project files.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13525 (prevent search_codebase from crashing the process on giant single-line files)
- **Category**: tool (search)
- **Size**: ALREADY SAFE (Alexi src/tool/tools/grep.ts L420-428 already processes ripgrep --json output line-by-line via chunk streaming: `proc.stdout?.on('data', (chunk: string) => { stdoutBuf += chunk; let idx: number; while ((idx = stdoutBuf.indexOf('\n')) !== -1) { const line = stdoutBuf.slice(0, idx); stdoutBuf = stdoutBuf.slice(idx + 1); handleLine(line); } })` — accumulates partial lines in `stdoutBuf` but drains complete lines incrementally, parses each JSON event separately L371-378 `JSON.parse(line)`, not vulnerable to unbounded buffering of all stdout; Cline's issue was buffering all events into one giant string before parsing, Alexi never does that, SKIP).

#### 8. Cline #13522: Hide per-tool MCP auto-approve checkboxes behind flag (LOW/SKIP)

- **What**: VS Code webview UI change hiding per-tool MCP auto-approve checkboxes behind feature flag `SHOW_MCP_PER_TOOL_AUTO_APPROVE=false`. The SDK approval path is all-or-nothing via the global \"Use MCP servers\" toggle, so the per-tool checkboxes were no-ops that implied control that doesn't exist. The flag preserves the checkbox components/handlers/RPC plumbing in case the SDK gains per-tool approval granularity later.
- **Why**: VS Code UI cleanup — remove no-op controls that confuse users.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13522 (hide per-tool MCP auto-approve checkboxes behind flag)
- **Category**: mcp (UI)
- **Size**: LOW (VS Code webview UI feature, Alexi is CLI-only with NO MCP approval UI or per-tool approval policies — src/mcp/ has server lifecycle via src/mcp/client.ts + transport via src/mcp/transport.ts but MCP tools execute without approval gates currently, pattern only relevant if Alexi adds MCP approval system where users can gate tool execution per-tool or per-server, SKIP for now).
